title: fix(mcp, lint): create_record and update_record over stdio answer droppedFields and no longer echo a dropped value; a flow write to a roll-up summary field draws a warning
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao6bxiPKCvVuzoFTExumbxoz)_

Fixes #35114

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：通过本机命令行方式接入 MCP 的 AI 调用方，新建或修改记录时若送了只读字段或汇总字段的值，回答里现在会列出被丢掉的字段，不再把没存下的值当成已存的值回给它；流程作者在流程里写汇总字段时，校验和构建会给出一条提醒（不会让构建失败）；文档补上了公开表单提交和克隆这两个同样会丢值的入口。
- 为什么做：这是汇总字段只读收口卡的三个后续小问题，替通过本机命令行接入 MCP 的调用方和写流程的作者补上「值被丢了却看不出来」的缺口。
- 出错会怎样：本机命令行方式的 MCP 回答多一个字段、少回显被丢的值，流程校验多一条提醒，存储与构建结果都不变；可直接撤回本 PR。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

**N1 — the stdio MCP bridge reports the drop.** `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`:

- `create` and `update` now pass an `onFieldsDropped` listener to `engine.insert` / `engine.update` and answer `droppedFields` exactly as the protocol's `createData` / `updateData` answer it behind the HTTP bridge: the engine's events as emitted, present only when at least one key was dropped (`droppedFieldsMember`).
- The answer's `record` no longer echoes a dropped caller value (`withoutDroppedKeys`): on `create` the payload fills only keys the write result omits and the engine did not drop; on `update` the read-path row stands for every dropped key.
- The update path had the same gap with the same shape, so it is fixed here too. It was the half where the echo was measured: `update_record` answered `biggest: 99` and `locked: 'forged'` over the stored `5` and `'kept'`.
- The stdio answer is not a published spec schema: `McpDataBridge.create` / `update` return `unknown`, and the tool answers the object as JSON. The member added is the one `CreateDataResponseSchema` / `UpdateDataResponseSchema` already declare for the HTTP answer. Output addition only; no tool input changes.

**N2 — the two missing doors are named** in `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` (the summary paragraph's door list). Measured on `origin/main` `ef39b2c191` by reading:

- public form submit (`packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts`): the context is `{ publicFormGrant, permissions, anonymous }`, never `isSystem`, so `createData` runs the engine's insert strip; the answer is `{ id, fields? }` only (#22437), so the drop is not shown to the submitter (`public-form-submit-answer.test.ts` already pins that `droppedFields` does not reach the answer);
- clone `overrides` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-crud.ts` `cloneData`): the source copy omits `summary` fields, `overrides` are assigned after that, and the insert runs with the `onFieldsDropped` listener, so a roll-up set through `overrides` is dropped and named in the clone's `droppedFields`.

The paragraph also says the MCP door covers create and update over HTTP and stdio. Triage 6969043738 ruled that N2 must not edit the consumed `.changeset/34672-*`; this PR does not touch it, and the new changeset does not restate the 18.6.0 entry (see Acceptance notes).

**N3, docs half — `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`.** The static `readonly` section now names the implicit roll-up lock: every `summary` field is read as `readonly: true` on create and update, dropped and reported under `readonly`, refused under `strictReadonlyWrites`, and that includes a flow's `create_record` / `update_record` without `runAs: 'system'`. Rule 1 (system context) still lets seed data, package installs and the recompute write it.

**N3, lint half — a warning, by the area ruling** (claim amendment 7035408057, option B). In `packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts`, a `create_record` / `update_record` node that does not run as `runAs: 'system'` and writes a `summary` roll-up that does not declare `readonly: true` now draws `flow-update-summary-field` (`FLOW_UPDATE_SUMMARY_FIELD`) at `warning`. Its message says the engine drops the value on create and update alike, and its hint names the node to remove the field from.

- The branch is flow-local: a private `summaryFieldIndex(stack)` over the objects as served. The shared `buildReadonlyIndex` and the hook and action readonly rules are unchanged.
- A roll-up that declares `readonly: true` still takes the static branch, so it is still `flow-update-readonly-field` at `error`. The same two gates as that branch hold: `runAs: 'system'` is not reported, and a create on an insert-strip-exempt object (`sys_`, platform-internal `managedBy`) is not judged.
- No build that passes today fails: this is a new warning, and no lint rule judged a summary write before (this is why the ruling chose B).
- Wiring: the constant is exported from the `@objectstack/lint` barrel (`index.ts`), and `os explain flow-update-summary-field` has an entry in `rule-explanations.ts`. Both files are outside the claim's file surface; the rule-explanations test requires every entry to be a barrel-exported id. `security.mdx` names the warning.

`.changeset/35114-stdio-mcp-dropped-fields.md`: `@objectstack/mcp` patch and `@objectstack/lint` patch. Under `Clause-②: yes`, per claim amendment 2 (7036853719): the new warning code and the new `@objectstack/lint` export widen the public surface, following the precedent of the `field/missing-value-domain` changeset. No build fails. Like every warning, it makes `os validate --strict` and `os lint --strict` exit 1, with no per-rule switch. The metadata save and publish answers carry it under `advisories` and never refuse on it: on a flow save whose user-run node writes such a roll-up, and on an object save that makes a field such a roll-up while a live user-run flow of the same package writes it. Read in the tree: `validate.ts` (`--strict` treats warnings as errors; `strictFailing` counts every non-`info` finding), `authoring-rules.ts` (`validateReferenceIntegrity`, `commands: ALL`), and `reference-integrity-suite.ts` (`validateReadonlyFlowWrites`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'object']`, `subjects: ['flows']`). In `runtime-gate.ts`, a non-error finding goes to `advisories`, on the subject pass too. `security.mdx` names both `--strict` runs beside "never blocks a build".

## Tests

`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.dropped-fields.test.ts` (new): a real `ObjectQL` over a row-keeping driver, the real stdio bridge, driven through the `create_record` / `update_record` tools:

- create: a `readonly: true` column and a `max` roll-up, both sent, are named in `droppedFields` (reason `readonly`), and neither value is in `record` or stored; control: a create sending neither answers no `droppedFields`;
- update: the same two are named, `record` carries the stored `'kept'` / `5`, and the store is unchanged; control: an update sending neither answers no `droppedFields`.

`packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.test.ts`, a new top-level `describe` for the roll-up:

- for `create_record` and `update_record`, a user-run write of the roll-up draws exactly one finding: `warning`, `flow-update-summary-field`, the exact path and `where`; the message says both verbs, on one line of at most 200 characters;
- controls: a declared `readonly: true` field (a roll-up and a text field) is still `flow-update-readonly-field` at `error`; a non-summary field draws nothing; a `runAs: 'system'` write of the roll-up on either verb draws nothing;
- the `os explain` entry names both verbs and says it never blocks a build.

<details><summary>Reverse verification and ablations (one-off, not kept)</summary>

- Whole-file revert of `stdio-data-bridge.ts` to `ef39b2c191` (blob `5cf5d500c8`, hash-checked before the run; restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, blob `bd2c6d16c6` equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty): `Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)`. The two pins were red (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'dfx_acct.biggest:readonly', … ]`) and the two controls green.
- Update echo, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `bd2c6d16c6` to `3d2bfef8e1`, restored equal to HEAD): `update_record` went red with `biggest: 99` / `locked: "forged"` received; `Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)`.
- Create echo, same tool (blob `bd2c6d16c6` to `c70446bc08`, restored equal to HEAD): stayed green, `4 passed`. The real engine's write result names every declared field (`null` where nothing was stored; a probe printed the result's keys), so on create the result already overwrites the echo. The create-side guard covers a write result that leaves such a key out; the test header says so.
- Lint, roll-up branch disabled (anchor `} else if (summaryFields?.has(fieldName) && !isSystemRun) {` prefixed with `false &&`; blob `848807de9c` to `546efd3591`, restored equal to HEAD): both verb pins red, `Tests  2 failed | 61 passed (63)`, every control green.
- Lint, system gate removed from that branch (blob `848807de9c` to `92cb50ff77`, restored equal to HEAD): both `runAs: 'system'` controls red, `Tests  2 failed | 61 passed (63)`.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The new changeset does not restate the 18.6.0 door list. AGENTS.md's Documentation Guardrails forbid an erratum to a released entry in a later one: a factual error in a released `CHANGELOG.md` entry is amended in that entry, in a dedicated docs-only PR. So the 18.6.0 door list is not restated here; amending the released `@objectstack/objectql` entry is a separate docs-only PR if the seat wants it.
- The new warning carries no `userTextParams` and no `.user-text.ts` catalog entry. A finding without them has no user sentence, so a save door shows its developer `message` (`finding-user-text.ts`: "a finding without `userTextParams` simply has no user sentence"). Translating it into the eleven platform locales is not in this card.
- The stdio answer still lacks the HTTP answer's `warnings`, `withheldMentions` and `notice` members. That is part of the divergence the bridge's header already lists ("spec-shaped receipts"). Not widened here.
- Accepted deviations from the contract review (record 7037237162), left as they are:
  - its N1: the `withoutDroppedKeys` comment says a `stored_expression` key's value comes from the write result. That holds on create; on update the bridge answers the value read before the write. That is no worse than before, when the caller's own value was echoed.
  - its N2: the new warning has no localised user sentence (see the note above). A Studio user sees the English developer `message`.

## Verification

- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/stdio-data-bridge.dropped-fields.test.ts`. Expect `Tests  4 passed (4)`. Then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.test.ts`. Expect `Tests  63 passed (63)`.
- Read first: `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` (`create` / `update` and the two helpers above `createStdioDataBridge`), then the roll-up branch in `packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts` (`summaryFieldIndex` and the `else if` before the `readonlyWhen` branch), then the two new test blocks.
